nodes.name: KxMoS2 crystals synthesis
nodes.procedure: After K2MoO4 (500 mg) and S powder (500 mg) were mixed and ground, the mixture was placed in a quartz tube and annealed in a tube furnace at 450°C for 1.5 h under a gas flow of H2 (10 s.c.c.m.) and Ar (190 s.c.c.m.). After cooling down to room temperature, the product was taken out and then mixed with S powder (500 mg). The obtained mixture was placed in a quartz tube and annealed in the tube furnace at 450°C for 1.5 h under atmosphere of H2 (10 s.c.c.m.) and Ar (190 s.c.c.m.). Subsequently, the reaction zone was heated to 850°C at a heating rate of 30°C min−1 under atmosphere of H2 (40 s.c.c.m.) and Ar (160 s.c.c.m.) and then maintained at 850°C for 10 h. After cooling down to room temperature, the obtained powder was collected and washed with Milli-Q water until the pH value of the suspension reached pH 7–8. The obtained powder was then stored in Milli-Q water for 24 h. After washing with Milli-Q water again and drying at room temperature under vacuum, the KxMoS2 crystals were obtained.

nodes.name: 1T'-MoS2 NSs electrochemical exfoliation
nodes.procedure: After the KxMoS2 crystals and PVDF as a binder were mixed in DMF, the mixture was uniformly coated on a copper foil and dried under vacuum, which was then used as the cathode. The mass ratio of KxMoS2 crystals, PVDF and DMF was 8:1:80. The graphite rod was used as the anode. The tetraheptylammonium bromide, which was dissolved in acetonitrile with a concentration of 5 mg ml−1, served as the electrolyte. The intercalation process was performed at an applied voltage of 8 V for 1 h. The intercalated sample was then transferred into a centrifuge tube followed by sonication in 5 ml of DMF for less than 5 s. The dispersion was centrifuged at 6,000 rpm for 10 min. The obtained precipitate was redispersed in 5 ml of Milli-Q water. The final product was collected by centrifugation at 6,000 rpm for 10 min and redispersed in Milli-Q water for further usage.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of 1T'-MoS2 NSs by electrochemical intercalation... redispersed in Milli-Q water for further usage.

nodes.name: 2H-MoS2 NSs electrochemical exfoliation
nodes.procedure: The intercalation and exfoliation to prepare 2H-MoS2 NSs were similar to the aforementioned processes used for preparation of 1T'-MoS2 NSs, except that the KxMoS2 crystals were replaced by the commercial 2H-MoS2 powder and the sonication time was prolonged to 30 min.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of 2H-MoS2 NSs by electrochemical intercalation... sonication time was prolonged to 30 min.

nodes.name: s-Pt/1T'-MoS2 photoreduction
nodes.procedure: 120 μl aqueous solution of 0.05 M K2PtCl4 was injected into 10 ml of a 1T'-MoS2 water–ethanol (vol/vol = 9:1) solution (0.10 mg ml−1; determined by ICP-OES) in a 15-ml glass vial. The obtained mixture was then irradiated under a 150-W halogen lamp at 10% of its full intensity for 14 h under ambient conditions. After the photoreduction reaction, the resulting solution was centrifuged at 6,000 rpm for 15 min. The precipitates were washed with IPA and collected for further usage.

nodes.name: PtNPs/2H-MoS2 photoreduction
nodes.procedure: The synthesis process was similar to that used for synthesis of the s-Pt/1T'-MoS2, except that the 1T'-MoS2 NSs were replaced by 2H-MoS2 NSs.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms distorted octahedral 1T′ structure and high crystallinity of 1T′-MoS₂ NSs with zigzag chains and Mo–Mo distance 2.78 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image shows the zigzag chains with the shortest Mo–Mo distance of 2.78 Å ... The corresponding fast Fourier transform pattern and the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern further confirm the distorted octahedral coordinated structure and the high crystallinity

nodes.evidence_snippet: The uniform elemental distribution of Mo and S elements with an Mo/S ratio of approximately 1:2 is confirmed by energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) (Supplementary Fig. 6).

nodes.evidence_snippet: No PtNPs can be observed on the surface of 1T′·MoS₂ (Fig. 2a)

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM reveals three types of single-atom Pt on 1T′-MoS₂: Pt_sub, Pt_ads·S, and Pt_ads·Mo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt atoms that were single-atomically dispersed on 1T′·MoS₂ occupy three different locations (Fig. 2c): Pt substituting the Mo site (Pt_sub), Pt adsorbed on the top site of S (Pt_ads·S) and Pt adsorbed on the top site of Mo (Pt_ads·Mo).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES white line height closer to PtS₂ than Pt foil, indicating oxidized Pt state in s-Pt/1T′-MoS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the height of the white line of Pt L₃-edge XANES of s-Pt/1T′-MoS is closer to that of PtS₂ and significantly higher than that of Pt foil, indicating the Pt species in the s-Pt/1T′·MoS₂ are dominantly in the oxidized state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed EXAFS shows dominant Pt–S peak at 1.87 Å (bond length 2.30 Å, coordination number 4.2), no Pt–Pt bond in s-Pt/1T′-MoS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed EXAFS of s-Pt/1T′·MoS₂ exhibits a dominant peak at 1.87 Å (Fig. 3b), which can be attributed to the Pt–S contribution. The fitting results demonstrate that the Pt–S bond has an average bond length of 2.30 Å and an average coordination number of 4.2

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f₇/₂ XPS peaks at 72.5 eV (Ptδ+), 73.5 eV (Pt²+), 74.8 eV (Pt⁴+) in s-Pt/1T′-MoS₂ confirming Pt–S bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the fitted peaks of Pt 4f₇/₂ of s-Pt/1T′-MoS₂ located at 72.5, 73.5 and 74.8 eV can be assigned to Ptδ+, Pt²+ and Pt⁴+, respectively, suggesting the formation of Pt–S bonds.
